We first aim to gain a fundamental understanding of the important parameters that can increase PCEs towards 28% which should allow us to develop and apply novel strategies to increase the stability of perovskite PV and de- risk perovskite PV for commercialization. Furthermore, the high throughput characterization tools that we are developing will accelerate the advancement of perovskite technology. The continued development of perovskite PV from MIT combined with our extensive experience with taking new technology to commercial products presents a unique opportunity to bring perovskites closer to commercialization. In addition to technological innovation and development, the talent development with the proposed project will be significant. This interdisciplinary project of material chemistry and electrical engineering will train researchers in this highly interdisciplinary and promising new area in semiconductor research. Project Schedule Status: Project is completed. Five Significant Project Achievements: 1. Chemical bath deposition (CBD) is widely used to deposit tin oxide (SnOx) as an electron- transport layer in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). In this work, a volatile oxalic acid (OA) is introduced as an alternative to TGA. OA, a dicarboxylic acid, functions as a chemical linker for the nucleation and attachment of particles to the substrate in the chemical bath. This rational design of a CBD SnOx layer leads to devices with T85 ≈1500 h, a significant improvement over the TGA- based device with T80 ≈250 h. The champion device reached a power conversion efficiency of 24.6%. This advancement is detailed in: Y. Lu, et al., “Rational Design of a Chemical Bath Deposition Based Tin Oxide Electron- Transport Layer for Perovskite Photovoltaics,” Adv. Mater. 35, 2304168 (2023). 2. We report bis(2-oxo-3-oxazolidinyl) phosphinic chloride (BOP-Cl) as a perovskite ink additive with the following benefits: (1) The phosphoryl and two oxo groups form six-membered intermolecular hydrogen-bonded rings with the formamidinium cation (FA), mitigating ion Page 7 of 54 DE-EE0009512 Massachusetts Institute of Technology migrations. (2) The hydrogen bonding reduces the electrophilicity of the ammonium protons by donating electron density, therefore reducing its reactivity with the surface oxygen on the metal oxide. Furthermore, the molecule can react to form a protecting group on the nucleophilic oxygen at the tin oxide transport layer surface through the elimination of chlorine. As a result, we achieve perovskite solar cells with an efficiency of 25.0% and improved MPP stability T93 of 1200 h at 40~45 °C compared to a control device with T86 of 550 h. This advancement is detailed in: Y. Lu, et al., “Stabilization of Organic Cations in Lead Halide Perovskite Solar Cells Using Phosphine Oxides Derivatives,” J. Am. Chem. Soc. 146, 32, 22387–22395 (2024). 3. We use measured responses from 368 devices to train a neural network (NN) with three optical inputs of constituent HOIP films (transmission, spectrally resolved photoluminescence, and time-resolved photoluminescence) to further predict the solar cell’s open-circuit voltage (Voc), short- circuit current (Jsc), and fill factors (FF).
